independence: Own reading of SPEC.md and workspace code; T5 outcomes from V4's oracle (X-02, X-01) and my re-score (X-03).
method: SPEC review; T5 tally across experiments (raw/t5_across_experiments.json); primary recomputed on the viol_noT5 outcome.
discrepancies: 'Silently': all 6 C runs state the device-offset reading in a code comment, and a02 lists it under 'Interpretation (implemented, flagged for confirmation)'. It is undocumented only under the QUESTIONS.md rule.

'May simply look specified' is only partly supported. All 6 K runs listed T5 in QUESTIONS.md as unspecified (for example a10: 'the spec does not say this outright. Alternative reading: UTC, or the store's time zone'), and so did a02 (C). They recognised the gap yet still implemented the device-local default. The better description is a strong natural default (Python's aware-datetime .weekday() gives device-local), not an apparent specification.
notes: Fairness judgment: T5 is a FAIR but LOW-DISCRIMINATION trap. SPEC D2-02 says placed_at carries 'the UTC offset reported by the customer's device' and that 'Customers order from many time zones'. This describes the data, not the rule, and R-08 never says whose calendar decides 'Saturday or Sunday' (device date, UTC date or a store time zone are all plausible). The fixture author treated it as unspecified: D2-03 had to add signed decision D-002 to settle it. Sonnet and one G run detected it. However, the SPEC wording and Python's default both point to device-local, and Haiku chose it in 24/25 runs regardless of arm. T5 therefore contributes nothing to the C-vs-K contrast, and excluding it leaves the primary unchanged.
